strings.note: Key on the shaker and glass benches' front strip that closes the bench and returns to the room. Keep the arrow and the two spaces after it. 8 px on a 196x46 key (~180 units of face): ~24 characters at most, one line.

The word on the bin key on the shaker and glass benches, under a drawn pedal bin. It shipped as the Turkish 'ÇÖP' in every language until 2026-09-17, when the author saw it in English. 16 px on an 80-unit face: ~5 characters.
Toast after the bin key throws the drink away and nothing is charged. One line.
Toast after the bin key throws a drink away at a cost. {fee} is the money lost with its currency sign, e.g. "$4" (the minus stays in the text). One line.

strings.text: TAKE THE LID OFF TO ADD IT
strings.note: Red readout line on the shaker bench when a bottle is picked from the cellar while the tin is capped and finished. 16 px, one line across the bench (~1250 units).

Words engraved under the nine growing rungs on the small plaque beneath the bottle's resting place on the shaker bench: the higher the bottle is lifted, the faster it pours. 8 px, one line in ~170 units: ~28 characters.

Caption engraved under the slim work column that stands left of the shaker-shaped measure on the shaker bench: it reads how far the shake or the stir has come. 8 px, centred under a 24-unit tube (~64 units of room): ~8 characters.
Appended to the shaker bench's readout while the tin is being shaken or stirred, after the figure so far: where the work is enough. {mark} is a percentage, e.g. "72%". 16 px, part of one line.
Red readout line on the shaker bench when a bottle is picked from the cellar while the tin still needs its lid. 16 px, one line.
Red readout line on the shaker bench when a bottle is picked from the cellar while the capped tin still needs mixing. 16 px, one line.
Shaker bench's standing hint once the tin is capped, for a drink that is shaken (the hint line is currently hidden; keep it short). 8 px, one line.
As bench.shaker.hint.shaken, for a stirred drink. 8 px, one line.

strings.text: THIS ONE IS BUILT — DO NOT WORK IT
strings.note: As bench.shaker.hint.shaken, for a built drink (no shaking or stirring). 8 px, one line.

strings.text: CAPPED — SHAKE IT, OR TAKE IT OVER
strings.note: Shaker bench's standing hint once the tin is capped and the drink names no method. 8 px, one line (hidden line).

strings.text: GRAB THE BOTTLE TO POUR · STIR IT, OR CAP IT AND SHAKE
strings.note: Shaker bench's standing hint while the tin is open and the drink names no method. 8 px, one line across the bench (hidden line).

strings.text: GRAB THE BOTTLE TO POUR · THIS ONE IS SHAKEN
strings.note: Shaker bench's standing hint while the tin is open, for a shaken drink. 8 px, one line (hidden line).

strings.text: GRAB THE BOTTLE TO POUR · THIS ONE IS STIRRED
strings.note: Shaker bench's standing hint while the tin is open, for a stirred drink. 8 px, one line (hidden line).

strings.text: GRAB THE BOTTLE TO POUR · THIS ONE IS BUILT — DO NOT WORK IT
strings.note: Shaker bench's standing hint while the tin is open, for a built drink. 8 px, one line (hidden line).

Step 1 of the four steps cut into the shaker bench's counter front (numbered socket, then the words). 8 px; the four steps share one 1100-unit line with ~28 units between them, so ~16 characters each.
Step 2 on the shaker bench's step strip: put the lid on the tin. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Step 3 on the shaker bench's step strip while the drink names no method. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Step 4 on the shaker bench's step strip: the drink moves on to the glass bench. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Step 3 on the shaker bench's step strip for a shaken drink. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Step 3 on the shaker bench's step strip for a stirred drink. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Step 3 on the shaker bench's step strip for a built drink (ticked on sight). 8 px, ~16 characters.
Caption under the standing shaker-shaped measure on the shaker bench: it measures the tin. 8 px, centred under a 136-unit measure: ~10 characters.

Caption beside each coloured band of the measure on both benches (shaker and glass), next to the bottle's small picture. {name} is the first word of the bottle's name in capitals (its data line); {share} is its share of the vessel, e.g. "45%". 8 px, white outlined, right-aligned in 170 units.

strings.text: shaker empty — tip the bottle over the tin
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while the tin holds nothing. 16 px, one line across the bench (~1250 units).
Shaker bench readout while the tin holds a drink. {fill} is how full the tin is, e.g. "60%"; {parts} is a comma-separated list of bench.shaker.line.part. 16 px, one line across the bench.
One ingredient in the shaker readout's list. {name} is the bottle's name in capitals (its data line); {share} is its share of the drink, e.g. "33%". Joined to the next with ", ".

strings.text: THE TIN IS FULL — PUT THE LID ON AND SHAKE, OR EMPTY IT
strings.note: Red readout line on the shaker bench while a bottle is tipped over a tin at the brim. 16 px, one line across the bench (~1250 units).
The shaker bench's (hidden) title when no bottle is in hand. 8 px, short.
Caption inside the work meter over the tin when the bench is opened on a tin already shaken. {pct} is the shake's thoroughness, e.g. "80%". Two spaces before it. 8 px inside a 260x22 tube.
Caption inside the work meter while the tin is being shaken. {pct} is the shake's thoroughness so far, e.g. "45%". Two spaces before it. 8 px inside a 260x22 tube.
Caption inside the work meter while the spoon is stirring. {pct} is the stir's thoroughness so far, e.g. "45%". Two spaces before it. 8 px inside a 260x22 tube.

strings.text: this one is STIRRED — work the spoon over the open tin
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while an open tin holds a stirred drink. The capital word is the method; keep it stressed. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: this one is SHAKEN — cap the tin, then shake it
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while an open tin holds a shaken drink. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: this one is BUILT — no shaking; cap it and take it over
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while an open tin holds a built drink. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: two spirits — stir it with the spoon, or cap it and shake
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while an open tin holds two spirits that must be mixed and no method is named. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: drag the lid onto the tin to close it
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while an open tin holds a drink with nothing else to say. 16 px, one line.
Shaker bench readout while the spoon is held over the tin. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: bring the spoon over the tin
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while the spoon is held away from the tin. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: it wants a mix — shake it, or bin it and start again
strings.note: Shaker bench readout while the tin is capped but the drink may not leave unmixed. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: IT BLEW UP — NEVER SHAKE A FIZZY DRINK
strings.note: Red readout line on the shaker bench while the tin bursts after a fizzy drink was shaken. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: lid off — the tin is open again
strings.note: Shaker bench readout after the TAKE THE LID OFF key. 16 px, one line.
Shaker bench readout after a stir is committed. {pct} is its thoroughness, e.g. "72%"; {line} is the tin's contents line (bench.shaker.line.contents). 16 px, one line across the bench.
Shaker bench readout after a shake is committed. {pct} is its thoroughness, e.g. "72%"; {line} is the tin's contents line (bench.shaker.line.contents). 16 px, one line across the bench.
Shaker bench readout when the empty tin is grabbed. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: cap it first — drag the lid onto the tin
strings.note: Shaker bench readout when the open tin is grabbed to shake. 16 px, one line.
Key under the capped tin that takes the lid back off. 8 px on a 160x52 key (~150 units of face): ~20 characters, one line.
Small readout at the left of the glass bench's counter front: the tin is empty. 8 px, 280 units.
Small readout at the left of the glass bench's counter front. {pct} is how much drink is left in the tin, e.g. "40%". 8 px, 280 units.
The glass bench's glass readout (currently hidden; the measure shows it). 8 px, 280 units.
The glass bench's glass readout (currently hidden). {pct} is how full the glass is, e.g. "60%". 8 px, 280 units.
The glass bench's glass readout when the glass is at the brim (currently hidden). 8 px.

strings.text: NOTHING IN THE TIN · PICK A BOTTLE AT THE BACK BAR
strings.note: Glass bench's line over the key strip when it opens with an empty tin. 16 px, one line across the bench (~1250 units).

strings.text: GRAB THE SHAKER · TIP IT OVER THE GLASS
strings.note: Glass bench's line over the key strip when it opens with a drink in the tin. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: THIS ONE NEEDS MIXING — BACK TO THE SHAKER
strings.note: Glass bench's line when the tin is tipped but its two spirits were never mixed. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: SHAKER EMPTY — FINISH IT AND SERVE
strings.note: Glass bench's line once the tin has poured everything into the glass. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: THE GLASS IS FULL — SERVE IT
strings.note: Glass bench's line once the glass is at the brim. 16 px, one line, amber.
Glass bench's live line while the tin pours dead over the glass. 16 px, one line.
Glass bench's live line while the tin pours a little off centre. 16 px, one line.
Glass bench's live line while the tin is tipped but aimed off the glass, so nothing pours. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: THE TIN IS OPEN — PUT THE LID ON AND MIX IT
strings.note: Glass bench's line when an uncapped tin is grabbed. 16 px, one line.
Step 1 of the two steps cut into the glass bench's counter front. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Step 2 on the glass bench's step strip. 8 px, ~16 characters.
Caption under the standing measure on the glass bench: it measures the glass. 8 px, centred under a 136-unit measure: ~10 characters.
The primary key on the glass bench: closes the bench with the drink ready to hand over. Keep the arrow. 16 px display face on a 250x46 key: ~14 characters.

strings.text: TILT TO 45° · STAND IT UP FOR HEAD
strings.note: Hint engraved under the draught bench's tilt ladder (nine rungs, one per ten degrees, lit as far as the glass leans; 45° fills fastest, upright pours foam). 8 px, wraps inside a 192-unit panel.
Word under the draught bench's PINT column (how full the glass is; a line marks the short-pour limit). 8 px, one short word.
Word under the draught bench's HEAD column (how much foam the pint carries; two lines mark the good band). 8 px, one short word.

strings.text: HOLD THE GLASS AND AIM · TILT IT TO FILL, HOLD IT STRAIGHT FOR FOAM · CLICK A KEG TO SWAP
strings.note: Standing instruction under the draught station's title. 8 px, one line across the top of the screen (~1280 units).
Key on the draught station that returns to the room. Keep the arrow and the two spaces after it. 8 px on a 196x46 key: ~24 characters, one line.
The primary key on the draught station: closes it with the pint ready; the player then clicks a drinker. 8 px on a 240x34 key (~232 units): ~28 characters, one line.
Step 1 on the draught bench's column (the list of four steps, one under another, as on the tin bench). 8 px, one short line, ~150 units.
Step 2 on the draught bench's column: hold the pint under the spout, leaning. 8 px, one short line.
Step 3 on the draught bench's column: straighten the glass to pour foam. 8 px, one short line.
Step 4 on the draught bench's column: press SERVE IT. 8 px, one short line.
The draught station's title and the keg's label when no keg is coupled. 16 px title / 8 px on the keg's ~80-unit label: ~10 characters.

strings.text: A COCKTAIL IS IN THE TIN — POUR IT OUT FIRST
strings.note: Draught station verdict line when a spare keg is clicked while a cocktail is being built. 16 px display face, outlined, one line across the screen.

strings.text: FINISH THE PINT IN THE GLASS BEFORE CHANGING KEGS
strings.note: Draught station verdict line when a spare keg is clicked over a glass holding another beer. 16 px display face, one line.

strings.text: tilt {tilt}° · pint {fill}% full · head {head}% · {left} left in the keg
strings.note: Draught station's small live readout. {tilt} is the glass's lean in whole degrees; {fill} and {head} are whole-number percents; {left} is what is left in the keg with up to one decimal (e.g. "2.5"). 8 px, one line across the screen.

strings.text: tilt {tilt}° · pint {fill}% full · head {head}% · {spilled} spilled · {left} left in the keg
strings.note: As bench.tap.readout, once beer has been spilled. {spilled} is the amount spilled with one decimal (e.g. "0.4"). 8 px, one line across the screen.
Draught station verdict while the glass is held away from the running tap. 16 px display face, outlined, one line.
Draught station verdict while the glass is tipped past the rim. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: ANOTHER BEER IS IN THE GLASS — SERVE IT OR BIN IT
strings.note: Draught station verdict when the glass holds a different beer from the keg on the line. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: TAKE THE GLASS TO THE TAP
strings.note: Draught station verdict while the glass is empty. 16 px, one line.

strings.text: THE GLASS IS FULL — LET IT SETTLE
strings.note: Draught station verdict when the glass is at the brim but the head is not yet right. 16 px, one line.
Draught station verdict: the pint is under three quarters full. 16 px, one line.
Draught station verdict: a full pint with a good head (plays the good chime). Must differ from the other verdicts. 16 px, one line.
Draught station verdict: too much foam (plays the bad chime). Must differ from the other verdicts. 16 px, one line.
Draught station verdict: too little foam (plays the flat chime). Must differ from the other verdicts. 16 px, one line.
The question the bin key hangs over itself in a small balloon on the first press; a second press while it stands throws the drink away (2026-09-22). One short line, ~10 characters at 16 px.
